output.review_comment:
The logic works and fixes the failing tests without editing them. The fixes for mixed case (e.g. "iPhone", "NASA") and for capitalizing the last word are general and match the docstring. The implementation is also sound: `result[-1].endswith(':')` correctly checks the previous word as it was emitted.

The problem is the colon rule. By the PR's own description, it contradicts the function's docstring. The docstring says a small word is capitalized only when it's the first or last word of the whole text. The new code also capitalizes small words after a colon, and the PR says this was added "only so that `test_subtitle_after_colon` passes." It isn't hardcoded to one input: capitalizing the first word of a subtitle is a standard title-case convention, and the teammate said the tests are the agreed editorial spec. So the behavior is probably right and the docstring is what's out of date. But as it stands, the code and its documentation disagree, which will confuse the next person who reads the function.

Requested changes:
1. Update the `title_case` docstring to describe the subtitle rule, e.g. "A small word is capitalized when it is the first or last word, or when it immediately follows a word ending in ':'". If it's unclear whether the editorial team intended this rule, confirm with the teammate.
2. Optional: say in the docstring that words with uppercase letters after the first character (including all-caps small words like "OF") are kept exactly as written, since the mixed-case check runs before the small-word check.
3. Clean up the PR description: drop the chat-style lines ("Perfect!", "✅") and describe the colon rule as spec rather than a test workaround.

Once the docstring matches the code, this is good to merge.
